prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Phoenix. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Phoenix for a dental implant?
engine_stated_criteria: “Can you give me an itemized estimate?”
“What implant system do you use, and will parts be available in the future?”
answer_verbatim:
For a dental implant in the Phoenix metro area, I’d make **2–3 consultation calls**, not just one. The best office depends on whether you need a single tooth, bone grafting, sedation, or a full-arch (“All-on-4”) solution.

Here are specific Phoenix-area practices worth calling:

| Practice | Best reason to call | Best fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Arizona Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons, P.C.** — Phoenix/Scottsdale-area offices | Oral and maxillofacial surgeons are the right people to assess difficult extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, sedation, and medically complicated cases. Ask whether the surgeon will place the implant and who will make the final crown. | Missing tooth with possible bone loss, prior failed implant, wisdom-tooth/extraction issues, IV sedation, or complex medical history. |
| **Arizona Periodontal Group** — Phoenix/Scottsdale metro | Periodontists specialize in gums, bone, and implant placement. A good option when gum disease, recession, or bone preservation is part of the problem. | You have gum disease, a tooth was lost due to periodontal disease, or you want an implant-focused second opinion. |
| **Midwestern University Dental Institute** — Glendale | Academic dental center with specialty departments and a team-based approach. Often a good place for a comprehensive evaluation when you may need surgery plus restorative work, and it can be less sales-driven than some implant-only chains. | You want an academic/specialty consultation, have a more complicated case, or are willing to trade some scheduling speed for a teaching-clinic model. |
| **A.T. Still University Arizona School of Dentistry & Oral Health clinics** — Mesa | Another academic option with faculty supervision and access to multiple specialties. Worth comparing if affordability and a carefully documented treatment plan matter. | Budget-conscious patients, complex cases, or people willing to travel to Mesa and potentially wait longer for appointments. |
| **ClearChoice Dental Implant Center – Phoenix** | Their model is built around full-mouth implant reconstruction, usually with imaging, surgery, and final teeth coordinated in one organization. It is especially relevant if you are considering a fixed full arch rather than one tooth. | Multiple failing/missing teeth, dentures, or interest in “All-on-4”/full-arch fixed teeth. Get at least one independent specialist quote too. |

## Who I would call first

### If you need **one implant for one missing tooth**
1. **Arizona Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons**
2. **Arizona Periodontal Group**
3. **Midwestern University Dental Institute**

This gives you two implant-surgery opinions plus an academic comparison. The important issue is not merely placing the implant—it is placing it in the correct position for the final crown and your bite.

### If you need **several implants or full-mouth reconstruction**
1. **ClearChoice Phoenix**
2. **Arizona Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons**
3. **Midwestern University Dental Institute** or **ATSU Mesa**

For a full-arch case, do not decide based only on a “monthly payment” or “same-day teeth” pitch. Get a written comparison of the provisional teeth, final teeth material, implant count, grafting, sedation, repairs, and long-term maintenance.

## What to ask each office on the phone

Use these questions to quickly separate strong implant practices from sales-oriented ones:

1. **“Will I get a CBCT/3-D scan before the final plan?”**  
   A proper implant plan commonly uses 3-D imaging, particularly in posterior upper jaw, lower jaw near nerves, grafting cases, and full-arch work.

2. **“Who places the implant, and who makes the final crown or bridge?”**  
   Ideally, the surgical and restorative providers coordinate from the beginning. Ask for the credentials of both clinicians.

3. **“Is the doctor an ABOMS-certified oral surgeon, an ABP-certified periodontist, or a prosthodontist?”**  
   You can independently verify specialty board credentials through the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, or American Board of Prosthodontics.

4. **“Can you give me an itemized estimate?”**  
   It should separately show:
   - consultation and 3-D imaging  
   - extraction, if needed  
   - bone graft or sinus lift, if needed  
   - implant fixture  
   - abutment  
   - final crown/bridge  
   - temporary tooth  
   - sedation  
   - follow-up and maintenance  

5. **“What implant system do you use, and will parts be available in the future?”**  
   A widely used, well-supported implant system is generally preferable to an obscure proprietary system.

6. **“If I need grafting or the implant does not integrate, what is covered and what would I pay?”**  
   Ask for the answer in writing. A “lifetime warranty” can exclude important costs such as grafting, anesthesia, lab fees, the final restoration, or treatment of infection.

## My practical recommendation

If you want the most balanced starting point, call:

- **Arizona Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons** for a surgical/complex-case opinion;  
- **Arizona Periodontal Group** for a gum-and-bone/implant-focused opinion; and  
- **Midwestern University Dental Institute** for a multidisciplinary academic comparison.

If you are considering replacing most or all teeth, add **ClearChoice Phoenix**—but compare its plan against at least one independent oral surgeon/prosthodontist or academic program before committing.

Before booking, confirm the current office location, implant provider, insurance participation, and whether the consultation includes a CBCT scan; staffing and office offerings can change.
